igcse-0580-indices-integer-laws.description: Read an index, join or cancel equal factors and recognise when a power repeats a whole group.

sections.title: What does an index count?
sections.label: Read an index
sections.intro: Think of an index as a short way to record repeated factors. Identify the base first. Everything inside a bracket may be the base. In this chapter you work with numbers. Indices II uses these rules to simplify algebra and find unknown indices.

blocks.html: In \(7^3\), the base is 7 and the index is 3. The value is \(7\times7\times7\). A base written by itself has index 1.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: When rewriting a repeated product, count the copies of the number. The multiplication signs separate the copies.

blocks.title: Read repeated factors
blocks.prompt: Write \(5\times 5\times 5\times 5\) as a single power of \(5\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
The same number, \(5\), is a factor 4 times. The base is \(5\).

The index records the number of copies. The expression is \(5^{4}\).
blocks.hint: Count the copies of the base, including the first one.

retry.feedback: You counted the multiplication signs. Count the factors on both sides of those signs.

blocks.html: \(7^3\) asks for three factors of 7. Multiplying \(7\) by \(3\) gives a different value.

blocks.title: Read repeated factors
blocks.prompt: Write \(8\times 8\times 8\) as a single power of \(8\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
The same number, \(8\), is a factor 3 times. The base is \(8\).

The index records the number of copies. The expression is \(8^{3}\).
blocks.hint: Count the copies of the base, including the first one.

retry.feedback: You counted the multiplication signs. Count the factors on both sides of those signs.

sections.title: When do I add the indices?
sections.label: Join equal factors
sections.intro: Look for multiplication between powers of the same base. Expanding a few small powers shows why their groups of factors join.

blocks.html: \(a^m\times a^n=a^{m+n}\) whenever the powers are defined. Keep the common base.

figure.alt: Four equal factors in the first group and three in the second group, joined by multiplication.
figure.caption: Each dot represents one factor. Joining the groups gives seven factors of the same base.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Read the first group and the second group. Add their counts of equal factors. Write the original base with this new index.

blocks.title: Multiply powers with the same base
blocks.prompt: Write \(6^{5}\times 6^{4}\) as a single power of \(6\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
\(6^{5}\) contains 5 copies of the base as factors. \(6^{4}\) adds 4 copies of the same base.

Join the two groups and keep the base: \(6^{5+4}=6^{9}\).
blocks.hint: The bases are the same. Count the factors in both groups together.

retry.feedback: Multiplying indices is for a power raised to a power. Here two separate powers are multiplied.

blocks.html: Check both the operation and the bases. Adding powers or multiplying powers with different bases does not give this rule.

blocks.title: Multiply powers with the same base
blocks.prompt: Write \(4^{4}\times 4^{5}\) as a single power of \(4\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
\(4^{4}\) contains 4 copies of the base as factors. \(4^{5}\) adds 5 copies of the same base.

Join the two groups and keep the base: \(4^{4+5}=4^{9}\).
blocks.hint: The bases are the same. Count the factors in both groups together.

retry.feedback: Multiplying indices is for a power raised to a power. Here two separate powers are multiplied.

sections.title: Which index do I subtract?
sections.label: Cancel equal factors
sections.intro: A fraction bar means division. In a quotient with the same non-zero base, pair up equal numerator and denominator factors. Each pair cancels to 1.

blocks.html: \(\dfrac{a^m}{a^n}=a^{m-n}\) when \(a\ne0\). Start with the numerator index.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Count the denominator factors being removed. Subtract this number from the numerator index. Read the result as a power of the original base.

blocks.title: Cancel equal factors in a quotient
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{5^{8}}{5^{6}}\) as a single power of \(5\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
Cancel 6 copies of \(5\) from the numerator with the 6 copies in the denominator.

The rest are in the numerator. Use \(5^{8-6}=5^{2}\).
blocks.hint: Subtract from the numerator index. The denominator index is the number of copies removed.

retry.feedback: You added the indices. In a quotient the denominator copies cancel.
The numerator is the starting group. Subtract the denominator index from it.

blocks.html: The numerator and denominator are ordered. Reversing the subtraction usually produces the reciprocal of the correct result.

blocks.title: Cancel equal factors in a quotient
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{8^{7}}{8^{2}}\) as a single power of \(8\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
Cancel 2 copies of \(8\) from the numerator with the 2 copies in the denominator.

The rest are in the numerator. Use \(8^{7-2}=8^{5}\).
blocks.hint: Subtract from the numerator index. The denominator index is the number of copies removed.

retry.feedback: You added the indices. In a quotient the denominator copies cancel.
The numerator is the starting group. Subtract the denominator index from it.

sections.title: When do I multiply the indices?
sections.label: Grouped power
sections.intro: An outer index on a bracket repeats the whole inner group. A power of a power has two levels, rather than two separate factors on the same line.

blocks.html: \((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\). There are \(n\) groups and each group contains \(m\) equal factors when both indices are positive integers.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Find the size of one group and the number of groups. Their product gives the new index.

blocks.title: Raise a power to another power
blocks.prompt: Write \((8^{4})^{5}\) as a single power of \(8\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
The outer index creates 5 groups. Each group contains 4 factors of \(8\).

There are \(4\times5=20\) factors of the original base. Write \(8^{20}\).
blocks.hint: Count the number of equal groups and the size of each group.

retry.feedback: The outer index repeats a whole group. Count all groups by multiplying the two indices.

blocks.html: Two powers next to a multiplication sign use the product rule. A power outside a bracket uses the power-of-a-power rule.

blocks.title: Raise a power to another power
blocks.prompt: Write \((5^{4})^{3}\) as a single power of \(5\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
The outer index creates 3 groups. Each group contains 4 factors of \(5\).

There are \(4\times3=12\) factors of the original base. Write \(5^{12}\).
blocks.hint: Count the number of equal groups and the size of each group.

retry.feedback: The outer index repeats a whole group. Count all groups by multiplying the two indices.

blocks.html: Underline the main operation before you choose a law. Give the requested form and write an exact value if asked to evaluate.

revision.body:
What does an index count?

In \(7^3\), the base is 7 and the index is 3. The value is \(7\times7\times7\). A base written by itself has index 1.

When rewriting a repeated product, count the copies of the number. The multiplication signs separate the copies.

When do I add the indices?

\(a^m\times a^n=a^{m+n}\) whenever the powers are defined. Keep the common base.

Read the first group and the second group. Add their counts of equal factors. Write the original base with this new index.

Which index do I subtract?

\(\dfrac{a^m}{a^n}=a^{m-n}\) when \(a\ne0\). Start with the numerator index.

Count the denominator factors being removed. Subtract this number from the numerator index. Read the result as a power of the original base.

When do I multiply the indices?

\((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\). There are \(n\) groups and each group contains \(m\) equal factors when both indices are positive integers.

Find the size of one group and the number of groups. Their product gives the new index.
revision.checks:
• Identify the base.
  • Check the operation and the sign of the index.
  • Use the answer form requested in the question.
revision.examTip: Two powers next to a multiplication sign use the product rule. A power outside a bracket uses the power-of-a-power rule.

igcse-0580-indices-zero-negative.description: Use cancellation to explain the zero index, take reciprocals for negative indices and read signs with brackets.

sections.title: Why does a zero index give one?
sections.label: Zero index
sections.intro: Divide a non-zero power by an identical power. Cancelling every matching factor leaves 1, and subtracting equal indices gives zero.

blocks.html: \(a^0=1\) for \(a\ne0\). Division by zero would not give the argument, so this rule does not define \(0^0\).

figure.alt: Three steps from one index above zero to one index below zero, each dividing the value by the base.
figure.caption: Dividing by the base takes the index down by one at each step.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: To check the value, write a same-base quotient with equal numerator and denominator indices. Compare the value of the quotient with the result of the index rule.

blocks.title: Follow the steps down
blocks.html:
IndexPowerExact value
\(3\)\(4^{3}\)\(64\)
\(2\)\(4^{2}\)\(16\)
\(1\)\(4^{1}\)\(4\)
\(0\)\(4^{0}\)\(1\)
\(-1\)\(4^{-1}\)\(\frac{1}{4}\)
\(-2\)\(4^{-2}\)\(\frac{1}{16}\)

blocks.title: Use the zero-index rule
blocks.solution:
The fraction \(\frac{10^{5}}{10^{5}}\) compares the same non-zero value with itself. Its value is 1.

The index rule gives \(10^{5-5}=10^{0}\). It follows that \(10^{0}=1\).
blocks.hint: A non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

retry.feedback: The index is zero. The value of the power is 1 for a non-zero base.

blocks.html: Zero names the index. It does not describe the value of a non-zero base raised to that index.

blocks.title: Use the zero-index rule
blocks.solution:
The fraction \(\frac{3^{4}}{3^{4}}\) compares the same non-zero value with itself. Its value is 1.

The index rule gives \(3^{4-4}=3^{0}\). It follows that \(3^{0}=1\).
blocks.hint: A non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

retry.feedback: The index is zero. The value of the power is 1 for a non-zero base.

sections.title: How does a negative index change the value?
sections.label: Negative index
sections.intro: Go down one index at a time by dividing by the base. After index zero, the next step gives the reciprocal of the base. Further steps add copies of the base in the denominator.

blocks.html: \(a^{-n}=\dfrac{1}{a^n}\) for \(a\ne0\). If \(a\) is positive, its reciprocal and its powers stay positive.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Write the reciprocal of the positive-index power. Evaluate that power exactly, then reduce the fraction if you can.

blocks.title: Evaluate a negative integer index
blocks.solution:
The negative index means take the reciprocal. Write \(4^{-2}=\frac{1}{4^{2}}\).

Evaluate the positive-index power below the fraction bar. The answer is \(\frac{1}{16}\).
blocks.hint: A negative index moves the positive-index power below a fraction bar.

retry.feedback: The minus sign is part of the index. Use the reciprocal, which stays positive for a positive base.
You evaluated the positive index. Now take its reciprocal.

blocks.html: The minus sign on an index asks for a reciprocal. It does not change a positive value into a negative value.

blocks.title: Evaluate a negative integer index
blocks.solution:
The negative index means take the reciprocal. Write \(7^{-2}=\frac{1}{7^{2}}\).

Evaluate the positive-index power below the fraction bar. The answer is \(\frac{1}{49}\).
blocks.hint: A negative index moves the positive-index power below a fraction bar.

retry.feedback: The minus sign is part of the index. Use the reciprocal, which stays positive for a positive base.
You evaluated the positive index. Now take its reciprocal.

sections.title: What belongs to the base?
sections.label: Bracketed base
sections.intro: A power outside brackets applies to the whole bracket. The group may be a fraction or an integer with a leading minus sign. Without brackets, a leading minus sign stays outside the power.

blocks.html: For non-zero \(a,b\), \(\left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right)^{-n}=\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)^n\). In \((-a)^{-2}\) the negative base is squared before its reciprocal is taken.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Identify the bracketed base before doing the calculation. For a negative index on a fraction, turn over the entire base fraction and then apply the positive index.

blocks.title: Use a negative index on a fraction
blocks.solution:
Find the reciprocal of the whole fraction, \(4\). The index is now \(3\).

Raise both parts of the reciprocal to that power. The result is \(64\).
blocks.hint: Turn the whole fraction over first, then apply the positive index to its numerator and denominator.

retry.feedback: The index is negative. Turn the fraction over before raising it to the positive power.
You took the reciprocal correctly. Now raise it to the positive power.

blocks.html: In \(-5^{-2}\), the power applies to 5 first and the leading minus gives \(-\dfrac1{25}\). In \((-5)^{-2}\) the sign is within the base.

blocks.title: Check where the minus sign belongs
blocks.solution:
The leading minus sign is outside the power. First evaluate the positive-base power: \(3^{-4}=\frac{1}{81}\).

Now apply the leading minus sign. The result is \(-\frac{1}{81}\).
blocks.hint: Check the brackets first. A minus sign outside the base is applied after the power.

retry.feedback: Look at the brackets. They tell you whether the first minus sign belongs to the base.

blocks.html: Underline the main operation before you choose a law. Give the requested form and write an exact value if asked to evaluate.

examples.title: Use the zero-index rule
examples.question: Work out the exact value of \(9^{0}\).
solution: The fraction \(\frac{9^{4}}{9^{4}}\) compares the same non-zero value with itself. Its value is 1.
The index rule gives \(9^{4-4}=9^{0}\). It follows that \(9^{0}=1\).

examples.title: Evaluate a negative integer index
examples.question: Work out the exact value of \(3^{-4}\).
solution: The negative index means take the reciprocal. Write \(3^{-4}=\frac{1}{3^{4}}\).
Evaluate the positive-index power below the fraction bar. The answer is \(\frac{1}{81}\).

examples.title: Evaluate a negative integer index
examples.question: Work out the exact value of \(6^{-4}\).
solution: The negative index means take the reciprocal. Write \(6^{-4}=\frac{1}{6^{4}}\).
Evaluate the positive-index power below the fraction bar. The answer is \(\frac{1}{1296}\).

examples.title: Use a negative index on a fraction
examples.question: Work out the exact value of \(\left(\frac{6}{7}\right)^{-2}\).
solution: Find the reciprocal of the whole fraction, \(\frac{7}{6}\). The index is now \(2\).
Raise both parts of the reciprocal to that power. The result is \(\frac{49}{36}\).

examples.title: Check where the minus sign belongs
examples.question: Work out the exact value of \((-9)^{-2}\).
solution: The brackets put the minus sign inside the base. Its positive even power is \(81\).
Take the reciprocal because the index is negative. The result is \(\frac{1}{81}\).

igcse-0580-indices-mixed-integer.description: Put several index rules in order, rewrite a numerical base to match another and keep addition separate from multiplication.

sections.title: How do I subtract a negative index?
sections.label: Signed subtraction
sections.intro: Keep each signed index together when copying it out of the expression. Subtraction remains the quotient rule even if a denominator index is negative.

blocks.html: For example, \(\dfrac{6^2}{6^{-3}}=6^{2-(-3)}=6^5\). Subtracting a negative index increases the resulting index.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Put brackets around signed indices. Subtract the denominator index from the numerator index. Simplify the signed calculation before deciding if a reciprocal is needed.

blocks.title: Subtract a signed index
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{3^{-1}}{3^{1}}\) as a single power of \(3\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
The powers have the same base. Use numerator index minus denominator index.

The index is \((-1)-(1)=-2\). The single power is \(3^{-2}\).
blocks.hint: Include the minus sign on the numerator index when you subtract.

retry.feedback: Division calls for subtraction. Adding would describe multiplication.
Subtract the denominator index from the numerator index in that order.

blocks.html: Changing the index of a denominator power may change the value of a quotient. Keep the denominator’s minus sign until you have written the subtraction.

blocks.title: Subtract a signed index
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{6^{-4}}{6^{-5}}\) as a single power of \(6\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:
The powers have the same base. Use numerator index minus denominator index.

The index is \((-4)-(-5)=1\). The single power is \(6^{1}\).
blocks.hint: Include the minus sign on the numerator index when you subtract.

retry.feedback: Division calls for subtraction. Adding would describe multiplication.
Subtract the denominator index from the numerator index in that order.

sections.title: Which rule comes first?
sections.label: Read the operations
sections.intro: In a quotient, simplify the whole numerator and denominator separately. This gives you two powers to compare rather than several competing operations.

blocks.html: In \(\dfrac{a^p\times a^q}{a^r}\), the numerator helps form \(p+q\). The denominator then changes the index to \(p+q-r\).

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Write a line for the numerator operation. Then subtract the denominator index. If you are asked to evaluate, turn a final negative index into a reciprocal.

blocks.title: Combine multiplication and division

sections.title: Can I rewrite the bases to match?
sections.label: Same numerical base
sections.intro: Read the base numbers before using any rule. If one is a power of the other, rewrite it and use the power-of-a-power rule to reveal a common base.

blocks.html: For \(36^3\) and \(6^4\), first use \(36=6^2\). The first power becomes \((6^2)^3=6^6\).

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Rewrite the larger base inside brackets. Multiply its inner and outer indices. Now compare the two same-base powers and choose the appropriate operation.

blocks.title: Rewrite one base to match the other
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{16^{4}}{4^{3}}\) as a single power of \(4\). Enter the index only.
blocks.solution:

Now the bases match. Divide by subtracting \(3\) from the numerator index, giving \(4^{5}\).
blocks.hint: Check whether the larger base is a power of the smaller base.

sections.title: What if I see addition or a product in brackets?
sections.label: Operation check
sections.intro: Check the main operation before deciding how to simplify. A plus sign between two powers tells you to add their values. A power on a product applies to each factor in that product.

blocks.html: \((ab)^n=a^nb^n\) for the numerical powers used here. By contrast, \(a^m+a^n\) does not combine by adding indices.

blocks.title: Method

blocks.title: Recognise when the product rule does not apply

The factors stay multiplied after taking their powers.

revision.body:
How do I subtract a negative index?

For example, \(\dfrac{6^2}{6^{-3}}=6^{2-(-3)}=6^5\). Subtracting a negative index increases the resulting index.

Put brackets around signed indices. Subtract the denominator index from the numerator index. Simplify the signed calculation before deciding if a reciprocal is needed.

Which rule comes first?

In \(\dfrac{a^p\times a^q}{a^r}\), the numerator helps form \(p+q\). The denominator then changes the index to \(p+q-r\).

Write a line for the numerator operation. Then subtract the denominator index. If you are asked to evaluate, turn a final negative index into a reciprocal.

Can I rewrite the bases to match?

For \(36^3\) and \(6^4\), first use \(36=6^2\). The first power becomes \((6^2)^3=6^6\).

Rewrite the larger base inside brackets. Multiply its inner and outer indices. Now compare the two same-base powers and choose the appropriate operation.

What if I see addition or a product in brackets?

\((ab)^n=a^nb^n\) for the numerical powers used here. By contrast, \(a^m+a^n\) does not combine by adding indices.

If the whole base is a product, give each factor the outer index. If two powers are added, evaluate separately or factorise a common factor.

igcse-0580-indices-fractional-extended.description: Read the root and power in a fractional index and find exact values for positive numerical bases.

sections.title: Extended · What root does the denominator give?
sections.label: Unit fraction index
sections.intro: With a positive base, a fractional index whose numerator is 1 asks for a root. Check the small number that tells you which root to take.

blocks.html: \(a^{\frac{1}{n}}=\sqrt[n]{a}\) for \(a>0\). Squaring the square root or cubing the cube root takes you back to the base.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Read the denominator and write the radical. Find the positive value that gives the original base when raised to that denominator.

blocks.title: Read a unit fractional index as a root
blocks.solution:
The denominator 4 names the root. Rewrite the expression as \(\sqrt[4]{4096}\).

The positive number \(8\) gives \(4096\) when raised to the power \(4\). So the root is \(8\).
blocks.hint: Find the positive number whose power gives this base.

retry.feedback: The requested root is the positive number. A root calculation does not ask for every solution of an equation.
The denominator of the index gives a root. It does not divide the base.

blocks.html: The denominator is the root order. It does not tell you to divide the base by that number.

blocks.title: Read a unit fractional index as a root
blocks.solution:
The denominator 4 names the root. Rewrite the expression as \(\sqrt[4]{81}\).

The positive number \(3\) gives \(81\) when raised to the power \(4\). So the root is \(3\).
blocks.hint: Find the positive number whose power gives this base.

retry.feedback: The requested root is the positive number. A root calculation does not ask for every solution of an equation.
The denominator of the index gives a root. It does not divide the base.

sections.title: Extended · Which comes first, the root or the power?
sections.label: Positive fraction index
sections.intro: The two numbers in a fractional index have different jobs. Taking the root first can keep the arithmetic much smaller.

blocks.html: \(a^{\frac{m}{n}}=(\sqrt[n]{a})^m\). The denominator gives the root. The numerator gives the power of that root.

figure.alt: The calculation proceeds from taking a root to raising a power, then taking a reciprocal only if the index is negative.
figure.caption: For a negative fractional index, take the reciprocal after using both parts of the fraction.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Find the root using the denominator. Write that result before raising it to the numerator power. Check that you carried out both steps.

blocks.title: Take a root before raising the power
blocks.solution:
The denominator 3 gives \(\sqrt[3]{512}=8\). Taking the root first keeps the number small.

The numerator 2 says to raise that root to the power \(2\). This gives \(8^{2}=64\).
blocks.hint: The denominator gives the root. The numerator gives the power on that root.

retry.feedback: This is the root step. Raise its result to the numerator power.
Take the root as well. Both parts of the fractional index matter.

blocks.html: A single root only finishes the calculation when the numerator is 1. If it is larger, you still have a power to apply.

blocks.title: Take a root before raising the power
blocks.solution:
The denominator 2 gives \(\sqrt{9}=3\). Taking the root first keeps the number small.

The numerator 3 says to raise that root to the power \(3\). This gives \(3^{3}=27\).
blocks.hint: The denominator gives the root. The numerator gives the power on that root.

retry.feedback: This is the root step. Raise its result to the numerator power.
Take the root as well. Both parts of the fractional index matter.

sections.title: Extended · Where does the reciprocal belong?
sections.label: Negative fraction index
sections.intro: A negative fractional index combines the root-and-power method with the negative-index rule. The sign acts on the whole value found using the positive index.

blocks.html: \(a^{-\frac{m}{n}}=\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt[n]{a})^m}\) for \(a>0\). Use the reciprocal as the final step.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Work out the root, apply the numerator power, then put the result under 1. If the bases match, the quotient rule also works with fractional indices. For example, \(\dfrac{125^{\frac23}}{125^{-\frac13}}=125^{\frac23-(-\frac13)}=125\).

blocks.title: Combine a fractional index and a negative sign
blocks.solution:
Use the positive index first. The cube root of \(27\) is \(3\).

Raise the root to the power \(2\) to get \(9\). The original index was negative, so the answer is the reciprocal \(\frac{1}{9}\).
blocks.hint: Root first, then positive power, then reciprocal.

retry.feedback: Your root and power give the correct denominator. Take the reciprocal.
A negative index means reciprocal. The original positive base keeps the value positive.

blocks.html: Taking the reciprocal of just the numerator of the exponent changes the question. Keep the root and power together before taking a reciprocal of their value.

blocks.title: Combine a fractional index and a negative sign
blocks.solution:
Use the positive index first. The square root of \(36\) is \(6\).

Raise the root to the power \(3\) to get \(216\). The original index was negative, so the answer is the reciprocal \(\frac{1}{216}\).
blocks.hint: Root first, then positive power, then reciprocal.

retry.feedback: Your root and power give the correct denominator. Take the reciprocal.
A negative index means reciprocal. The original positive base keeps the value positive.

sections.title: Extended · What if the base is already a fraction?
sections.label: Fraction base
sections.intro: When a whole fraction is inside brackets, both numerator and denominator are part of the base. A root can act on both if their individual roots can be found.

blocks.html: For positive \(a,b\), \(\sqrt[n]{\dfrac{a}{b}}=\dfrac{\sqrt[n]{a}}{\sqrt[n]{b}}\). The following power then acts on both parts of that fraction.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.html: Take the appropriate root of the numerator and denominator. Raise this fraction to the numerator power of the index. Only take a reciprocal if the original index was negative.

blocks.title: Evaluate a fractional index of a fraction
blocks.solution:
The denominator of the index is 2. Take that root of both the numerator and denominator of the base. The root is \(\frac{2}{5}\).

Raise the root to the power \(3\), giving \(\frac{8}{125}\). Take its reciprocal to get \(\frac{125}{8}\).
blocks.hint: Apply the root to the whole base fraction. Then use the numerator of the index and check its sign.

retry.feedback: The original index is negative. The final answer is the reciprocal of that power.
You found the root. Apply the numerator power and check the sign of the index.

blocks.html: Check what the brackets contain before taking a root. Applying the root to just the numerator leaves part of the base unchanged.

blocks.title: Evaluate a fractional index of a fraction
blocks.solution:
The denominator of the index is 3. Take that root of both the numerator and denominator of the base. The root is \(\frac{5}{8}\).

Raise the root to the power \(2\), giving \(\frac{25}{64}\). Take its reciprocal to get \(\frac{64}{25}\).
blocks.hint: Apply the root to the whole base fraction. Then use the numerator of the index and check its sign.

retry.feedback: The original index is negative. The final answer is the reciprocal of that power.
You found the root. Apply the numerator power and check the sign of the index.
